ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the straight wire ab is located in the plane of the paper; the wire goes obliquely from the lower-left end a to the upper-right end b, and its length is labeled l. The uniform magnetic field \vec{B} is represented by multiple horizontal rightward arrows, also in the plane of the paper. The velocity \vec{v} of the wire is represented by an arrow obliquely toward the lower right, likewise located in the plane of the paper, and making an angle a with the direction of the magnetic field. Reasoning: The motional electromotive force in the moving wire is ε = ∫(\vec{v} × \vec{B}) · d\vec{l}. Since both \vec{v} and \vec{B} are in the plane of the paper, the direction of \vec{v} × \vec{B} is perpendicular to the plane of the paper; whereas the wire ab and the line element d\vec{l} are both in the plane of the paper. Therefore (\vec{v} × \vec{B}) has no component along the wire ab, the dot product is 0 everywhere, so the result of the integral is 0.
